package_info.package_name: PowerTrash Loader (delivered via CVE-2022-22954 exploit chain)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware delivered via remote code execution, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects VMware Workspace ONE Access and related products vulnerable to CVE-2022-22954, CVE-2022-22957, CVE-2022-22958)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack chain is malicious because it exploits a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2022-22954) in VMware Workspace ONE Access and related products to execute arbitrary code, downloads and runs a highly obfuscated PowerShell loader (PowerTrash) from an attacker-controlled server, and injects a post-exploitation agent (Core Impact) into memory, enabling persistent remote control, lateral movement, and further exploitation of the compromised environment.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (triggered via remote code execution exploit)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the vulnerable VMware service process (e.g., Identity Manager web service process memory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is executed via remote code execution, launches a PowerShell process with no profile and hidden window, downloads a remote script from the attacker's C2 server using DownloadString, and immediately executes it in memory using Invoke-Expression (IEX), resulting in the execution of attacker-supplied code on the compromised VMware service process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This command is highly suspicious because it uses PowerShell with flags to evade detection (-nop, -w hidden), downloads code from an external, attacker-controlled server, and executes it directly in memory, which is a common initial access and staging technique for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VMware service processes should never invoke PowerShell to download and execute remote scripts, especially with obfuscation and evasion flags.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use similar PowerShell commands for remote management or automation, but only in strictly controlled, logged, and authorized maintenance scenarios, never from a production VMware service process.
key_indicators: PowerShell process launched with -nop (no profile) and -w hidden (window hidden) flags
Use of DownloadString to retrieve code from an external C2 server
Immediate execution of downloaded code via Invoke-Expression (IEX)
PowerShell process parented by a VMware service process

execution_context.file_location: Process memory (downloaded and executed in-memory by the stager PowerShell script)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: <Highly obfuscated PowerTrash loader PowerShell code, downloaded from C2 server>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the stager script executes, the highly obfuscated PowerTrash loader PowerShell code is downloaded from the attacker's C2 server and executed in memory, which then downloads the Core Impact agent and injects it into the process memory, establishing a persistent backdoor and command-and-control channel for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of highly obfuscated PowerShell code that performs in-memory execution and process injection to load a post-exploitation agent is a hallmark of advanced malware and red team tools, designed to evade detection and maintain persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not use obfuscated scripts to perform in-memory code execution, process injection, or establish unauthorized command-and-control channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Red team or penetration testing engagements may use similar techniques for authorized security assessments, but such activity should never occur in production environments without explicit authorization and monitoring.
key_indicators: Obfuscated PowerShell code executed in memory
Process injection to load a post-exploitation agent (Core Impact)
No persistent files written to disk; all activity occurs in memory
Network communication to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Exploit CVE-2022-22954 to achieve remote code execution on the VMware service process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the vulnerable VMware service process

attack_chain.action: Execute a PowerShell stager that downloads and runs a remote script from the attacker's C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and in-memory execution of the PowerTrash loader

attack_chain.action: Run the highly obfuscated PowerTrash loader, which downloads and injects the Core Impact agent into process memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of a persistent command-and-control channel and full remote control of the compromised system

behavioral_signatures: PowerShell process execution with -nop (no profile) and -w hidden (window hidden) flags, especially when parented by VMware service processes
PowerShell downloading and executing remote scripts using DownloadString and Invoke-Expression (IEX)
In-memory execution of highly obfuscated PowerShell code
Process injection and in-memory loading of post-exploitation agents (e.g., Core Impact)
Absence of persistent malware files on disk; all malicious activity occurs in memory
file_indicators: No persistent malicious files; all code executed in memory
Unusual PowerShell process invocation by VMware service processes (e.g., Identity Manager web service)
Unexpected child PowerShell processes spawned by VMware service accounts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from VMware service processes to suspicious or unknown external C2 domains/IPs
Connections to known Core Impact C2 infrastructure
Unusual network activity from VMware servers not associated with legitimate updates or operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PowerShell processes spawned by VMware service accounts, especially those using -nop and -w hidden flags. Detect and alert on network connections from VMware servers to external IPs or domains not associated with legitimate VMware operations. Analyze process trees for PowerShell child processes of VMware services. Use memory scanning to identify in-memory execution of obfuscated PowerShell code and process injection behaviors. Correlate logs for exploitation attempts of CVE-2022-22954 and related vulnerabilities, and cross-reference with known Core Impact C2 infrastructure.
